# Workspace Boundaries & Handoff Protocol

The `basketiq` workspace (`/Users/jjdelcampo/projects/basketiq`) is the only active IDE workspace. All repos live under this directory.

## Workspace structure

```text
/Users/jjdelcampo/projects/basketiq/
  basketiq-wow/          # rules, config, workflows, skills — single source of truth
  biq-app/               # app shell (PWA + BFF)
  biq-onboard/           # auth-to-club onboarding, club/membership management
  biq-social/            # club news/social service
  biq-methodology/       # methodology authoring and governance
  biq-season-plan/       # season planning
  biq-cycle/             # objective progression + session planning
  biq-training/          # trainings
  biq-playbook/          # tactical board
  biq-chronicle/         # match chronicle
  biq-knowledge/         # knowledge/extraction backend
  biq-mcp/               # MCP server for BasketIQ business services
  biq-e2etests/          # E2E test suite
  biq-admin/             # admin tooling
  handoff/               # handoffs between roles (Architect ↔ Developer)
    inbox/
    processed/
    outbox/
```

## Handoff lifecycle

Handoffs are the canonical mechanism for passing work between roles (Architect ↔ Developer).

### Structure

```text
/Users/jjdelcampo/projects/basketiq/handoff/
  inbox/       # incoming, pending
  outbox/      # outgoing, sent
  processed/   # completed, archived
```

These folders are **local, not versioned in git**. Create them if missing.

### Naming

```text
YYYY-MM-DD-<intent-slug>-from-<source>.md
```

- `intent-slug` briefly describes the action/topic (kebab-case).
- `source` is the emitting role or agent (e.g., `architect`, `developer`).

### Boundary rules

- The workspace is shared. All repos are readable.
- Before broad searches, scope to the owning repo or subdirectory.
- Do not use auxiliary clones or worktrees as an editing surface without explicit authorization.

### Forbidden

- Versioning `handoff/` content in git.
- Deleting processed handoffs instead of moving them to `processed/`.
- Leaving completed handoffs in `handoff/inbox/`.
- Mass-grepping the whole workspace when the task belongs to a specific repo.
- Indexing `_local_ops`, E2E artifacts, dumps, backups, `dist`, `node_modules` or venvs as if they were source code.

## Inter-Role Handoff Protocol

### 1. Principle

If it concerns you, **it is in your `inbox/`**. The `handoff/inbox/` is the canonical entry folder.

### 2. Handoff types

**Phase handoff** — the Architect hands a phase to the Developer:

```text
Phase handoff — Phase <N>: <title>
From: Architect
To: Developer
Design doc: <path to the design document in handoff/inbox/>
Scope: <what this phase implements>
Acceptance criteria: <how we know the phase is complete>
Dependencies: <prior handoffs or artifacts needed>
References: <absolute paths to relevant files>
```

**Review request** — the Developer delivers evidence to the Architect:

```text
Review request — Phase <N>: <title>
From: Developer
To: Architect
PR: <PR URL>
CI run: <CI run URL>
Tests: <exact command(s) + result>
Evidence file: <path to the evidence file>
Live verification: <request/response, trace, deploy run_id — if applicable>
```

**Review verdict** — the Architect replies to the Developer:

```text
Review verdict — Phase <N>
From: Architect
To: Developer
Verdict: APPROVED | APPROVED_WITH_NOTES | CHANGES_REQUESTED
PR: <PR URL>
Notes: <if APPROVED_WITH_NOTES — non-blocking observations>
Changes needed: <if CHANGES_REQUESTED — file/line/why/direction>
Next phase handoff: <if APPROVED — path to the next phase handoff in handoff/inbox/>
```

**Dependency request** — one role requests a dependency from another:

```text
Dependency request
Owner: <responsible role/area>
Needed by: <consuming role> - <phase>
Need: <contract/data/criteria/queue/event>
Why: <which decision or implementation it unblocks>
Acceptance criteria: <how we know it serves>
Unblocks: <unblocked phase>
```

**Dependency completed** — when a dependency is delivered:

```text
Dependency completed
Producer: <producing role>
Consumer: <consuming role>
Delivered artifact: <schema/fixture/model/event/doc>
How to use: <consumption steps or contract>
Validation: <tests/fixtures/dry-run>
```

### 3. Processing flow

When a role finds a new document in its `handoff/inbox/`:

1. Read it before closing or communicating in-flight work.
2. Register it in its live plan/registry as a dependency or received phase.
3. Execute the requested work (Developer) or audit the evidence (Architect).
4. When integrated, **move** it from `handoff/inbox/` to `handoff/processed/` (never delete).

**Close-of-work rule:** before announcing that a piece of work is finished, every role **must check its own `handoff/inbox/`**.

### 4. Forbidden (inter-role protocol)

- Creating a handoff in your own `handoff/inbox/` expecting someone else to pick it up.
- Moving other roles' handoffs to `processed/`.

## Task close-out

When finishing, the agent must make clear:

- Which logs/handoffs contain evidence.
- Whether authorized cross-paths were used and need documenting.
- Whether heavy artifacts were generated and where they are excluded or stored.
